# Private Limited Company Incorporation: India vs. Estonia vs. Delaware
## Comparative Research Report for Founders — November 2026

---

## Executive Summary

A founder choosing between India, Estonia, and Delaware faces markedly different regulatory environments. **Estonia** is the fastest and simplest path to a fully digital private company (OÜ): one state fee of €265, approval in one working day, and no ongoing annual report filing fee — though a contact-person service (~€200–400/yr) is effectively mandatory for non-residents [11][13]. **Delaware LLC** is the fastest US option: one filing fee of $110, no annual report, and a flat $400/yr tax, though a registered agent (private cost, government fees set) is legally required [34][5][35]. **India** is the most complex: 5–6 sequential steps, fees that vary by share capital and state (stamp duty), and the richest ongoing compliance calendar — but it is the only option for a company that must actually operate on the ground in India [26][40].

---

> **Important fee caveat:** MCA waived incorporation government fees (ROC registration fee) for companies with authorised capital up to ₹15 lakh via the SPICe+ zero-fee scheme introduced 26 January 2019. The MCA "Enquire Fees" page notes all displayed figures are "indicative only" [9]. The binding fee is computed live at the time of SPICe+ filing. Stamp duty on MOA/AOA is a **State** levy, not a central fee, and varies sharply by state [40][45].

Because the tax is paid in arrears, the **first $400 payment is due June 1, 2027** (covering tax year 2026). The payment due June 1, 2026 (covering tax year 2025) remained $300 [15][17][23][24]. The official Division of Corporations LLC/LP/GP franchise tax instructions page and the official LLC Formation PDF both state **$400** as the current annual tax [5][34].

> **Corporation franchise tax note:** HB 400 did **not** increase the standard annual franchise tax rates for domestic corporations. Corporations may still see higher costs from increases to filing fees, annual report fees, and expedited service charges [15].

---

## Side-by-Side Summary Table

| Dimension | India (Pvt Ltd) | Estonia (OÜ) | Delaware LLC | Delaware C-Corp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Total minimum govt fees at incorporation** | ~₹1,131 (name ₹1,000 + PAN/TAN ~₹131, authorised capital ≤ ₹15 lakh, **excl. state stamp duty**) [19][39] | **€265** (state fee) [11][13] | **$110** [27][34] | **$109 minimum** (varies by stock) [27] |
| **Stamp duty / additional mandatory govt costs** | Varies by state; UNCLEAR without knowing registered-office state. Example: Delhi ≈ 0.15% of authorised capital [41] | None at incorporation | None | None |
| **e-Residency / prerequisite cost** | DSC from private CA (no govt fee) | €150 (e-Residency, if non-Estonian) [13] | None | None |
| **Number of steps to incorporation** | **6–8** (DSC → DIN → Name → SPICe+ B → AGILE-PRO-S → Stamp duty → PAN/TAN → INC-20A) | **4–7** (e-Residency optional → name check → prepare app → pay share capital → sign → pay €265 → submit) [12] | **3–4** (name check → appoint agent → file Certificate of Formation) | **3–4** (name check → appoint agent → file Certificate of Incorporation) |
| **Official time to incorporation approval** | ~4 working days (2 WD name + 2 WD COI) if no deficiencies [36] | **~1 working day** [12][20] | UNCLEAR — no official SLA for standard processing; expedited options from 1 hour [6] | UNCLEAR — same as LLC |
| **Annual govt fees (ongoing)** | ₹200–₹600 × 2 forms (AOC-4 + MGT-7) = ₹400–₹1,200/yr minimum (more if late) [39] | **Nil** (no annual report state fee) [14] | **$400/yr** (LLC annual tax, due June 1) [5][34] | **$50** (annual report) + min. **$175** franchise tax = **$225 minimum/yr** [3][7] |
| **Ongoing compliance complexity** | High (AOC-4, MGT-7, DIR-3 KYC, statutory audit, AGM, INC-20A, possible GST/EPFO/ESIC) | Low-moderate (annual report mandatory, no state fee; accounting required) | Low (flat annual tax only; no annual report) | Moderate (annual report + franchise tax by March 1) |
| **Registered agent / contact person required** | No (ROC address system) | Yes — contact person for e-residents (~€200–400/yr private cost) [13] | Yes — Delaware registered agent (private cost, UNCLEAR govt-set fee) [34][35] | Yes — Delaware registered agent (same) [2][35] |
| **Foreign founder can incorporate 100% online** | Yes (with Indian DSC from listed CA; at least 1 resident director required) [26] | **Yes** (with e-Residency or eligible EU ID) [11][12] | **Yes** (via registered agent service; no residency requirement) | **Yes** (via registered agent service) |
| **Resident director requirement** | **Yes** — at least 1 director must have resided in India for ≥182 days in the previous calendar year [29] | No residency requirement for directors | None | None |

---

## Recommendation: Easiest Place to Start

### **Recommended: Estonia (OÜ) for a non-India-based founder; Delaware LLC for a US-operations founder**

**For a founder with no specific India nexus:** **Estonia** is the objectively simplest and fastest path:

- **One state fee** (€265), **one government step**, **one working day** to approval [11][12][20]
- No minimum capital beyond €0.01 [11]
- 100% digital — 15-minute application if documents are in order [20]
- No annual report filing fee [14]
- 0% corporate tax on retained/reinvested profits [20]
- No residency requirement for directors or shareholders

**For a founder targeting the US market or seeking VC funding:** **Delaware LLC** (or C-Corp for VC-backed startups) is standard. The LLC has the simplest ongoing burden ($400 flat annual tax, no annual report) [5][34].

**India is not "easiest" but is non-negotiable** if the company must operate physically in India — a foreign-registered company cannot substitute for an Indian entity when Indian regulatory compliance, GST registration, employment contracts, or Indian banking are needed.

---

## Trade-offs of Estonia (Easiest Choice)

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Speed & simplicity ✅** | 1 working day to approval; 1 fee; fully digital [12][20] |
| **Cost ✅** | €265 at formation; no annual report fee [13][14] |
| **Tax efficiency ✅** | 0% on reinvested profits; 20% only on distributions from 2026 [13][20] |
| **e-Residency prerequisite ⚠️** | Non-EU founders must pay €150 for e-Residency and wait for card delivery before incorporation [13] |
| **Contact person cost ⚠️** | Effectively mandatory for non-residents: ~€200–400/yr private cost [13] |
| **Accounting cost ⚠️** | Annual report mandatory even for inactive companies; accountant from ~€50/month [13][14] |
| **Banking ⚠️** | Opening a business bank account from outside Estonia can be difficult; some founders use fintech alternatives (Wise, Revolut Business) — no official government source on this, UNCLEAR |
| **No physical presence benefit** | Estonian OÜ does not substitute for local registration in India or most US states if you operate there |
| **Limited VC ecosystem** | Estonian companies are less familiar to US VCs than Delaware corporations; if raising US institutional capital, a Delaware C-Corp may be preferred |
| **Activity licences** | Regulated sectors require additional licences from Estonian authorities [12] |

---

## Source Reliability Notes

- **India fees:** The MCA "Enquire Fees" page states all figures are "indicative only" [9]. The binding fee schedule is the Table of Fees in the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014 as amended [40], and the live SPICe+ computation. MCA processing times are from a secondary source reporting MCA-published SLAs [36]; no primary MCA SLA page was accessible in the evidence set — treat these as reported, not verified from a live official page.
- **Estonia:** Key facts (€265 fee, 1-working-day processing, annual report deadline) are confirmed across multiple primary official sources [11][12][13][14][20].
- **Delaware:** Incorporation fees post-August 2026 are confirmed by the official Division of Corporations fee schedule PDF dated August 1, 2026 [27] and the official LLC Formation PDF [34]. Annual tax of $400 for LLCs is confirmed by multiple official Delaware sources [3][5][34] and corroborated by multiple secondary sources [15][17][23]. One low-quality source dated July 2026 still cited $300 [44], which appears to reflect the pre-2026-tax-year rate.
- **Standard processing time for Delaware:** The Division of Corporations does not publish an official standard (non-expedited) SLA for Certificate of Formation/Incorporation on the pages reviewed. Only expedited service times are officially stated [6]. This is **UNCLEAR** for standard filing.

# Private Limited Company Incorporation: India vs. Estonia vs. Delaware
## Comparative Research Report for Founders — November 2026

---

## Executive Summary

A founder choosing between India, Estonia, and Delaware faces markedly different regulatory environments. **Estonia** is the fastest and simplest path to a fully digital private company (OÜ): one state fee of €265, approval in one working day, and no ongoing annual report filing fee — though a contact-person service (~€200–400/yr) is effectively mandatory for non-residents [11][13]. **Delaware LLC** is the fastest US option: one filing fee of $110, no annual report, and a flat $400/yr tax, though a registered agent (private cost, government fees set) is legally required [34][5][35]. **India** is the most complex: 5–6 sequential steps, fees that vary by share capital and state (stamp duty), and the richest ongoing compliance calendar — but it is the only option for a company that must actually operate on the ground in India [26][40].

---

## Section 1: India — Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd)

### Governing Law & Authority
Companies Act, 2013; Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA); Registrar of Companies (ROC). Primary portal: [mca.gov.in](https://www.mca.gov.in).

> **Important fee caveat:** MCA waived incorporation government fees (ROC registration fee) for companies with authorised capital up to ₹15 lakh via the SPICe+ zero-fee scheme introduced 26 January 2019. The MCA "Enquire Fees" page notes all displayed figures are "indicative only" [9]. The binding fee is computed live at the time of SPICe+ filing. Stamp duty on MOA/AOA is a **State** levy, not a central fee, and varies sharply by state [40][45].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** | Each proposed director must obtain a Class 3 DSC from an MCA-listed Certifying Authority. Required to digitally sign all MCA e-forms. Foreign directors must use an Indian CA [26]. | No MCA government fee; DSC cost paid to private Certifying Authority. UNCLEAR — no government fee set by MCA for DSC itself. | UNCLEAR — set by private CA, typically 1–3 days. | https://www.mca.gov.in/content/mca/global/en/mca/fo-llp-services/enquire-fees.html [9] |

Under SPICe+, DIN is bundled at no additional charge. | ₹500 per DIN (separate DIR-3 filing); **Nil if allotted via SPICe+** [39] | 1 working day (inform deficiencies: 1 WD; approve: 1 WD) [36] | https://ca2013.com/rule-12-companies-registration-offices-and-fees-rules-2014/ [39]; https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/mca-processing-time [36] |

## Recommendation: Easiest Place to Start

### **Recommended: Estonia (OÜ) for a non-India-based founder; Delaware LLC for a US-operations founder**

**For a founder with no specific India nexus:** **Estonia** is the objectively simplest and fastest path:

- **One state fee** (€265), **one government step**, **one working day** to approval [11][12][20]
- No minimum capital beyond €0.01 [11]
- 100% digital — 15-minute application if documents are in order [20]
- No annual report filing fee [14]
- 0% corporate tax on retained/reinvested profits [20]
- No residency requirement for directors or shareholders

**For a founder targeting the US market or seeking VC funding:** **Delaware LLC** (or C-Corp for VC-backed startups) is standard. The LLC has the simplest ongoing burden ($400 flat annual tax, no annual report) [5][34].

**India is not "easiest" but is non-negotiable** if the company must operate physically in India — a foreign-registered company cannot substitute for an Indian entity when Indian regulatory compliance, GST registration, employment contracts, or Indian banking are needed.

## Trade-offs of Estonia (Easiest Choice)

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Speed & simplicity ✅** | 1 working day to approval; 1 fee; fully digital [12][20] |
| **Cost ✅** | €265 at formation; no annual report fee [13][14] |
| **Tax efficiency ✅** | 0% on reinvested profits; 20% only on distributions from 2026 [13][20] |
| **e-Residency prerequisite ⚠️** | Non-EU founders must pay €150 for e-Residency and wait for card delivery before incorporation [13] |
| **Contact person cost ⚠️** | Effectively mandatory for non-residents: ~€200–400/yr private cost [13] |
| **Accounting cost ⚠️** | Annual report mandatory even for inactive companies; accountant from ~€50/month [13][14] |
| **Banking ⚠️** | Opening a business bank account from outside Estonia can be difficult; some founders use fintech alternatives (Wise, Revolut Business) — no official government source on this, UNCLEAR |
| **No physical presence benefit** | Estonian OÜ does not substitute for local registration in India or most US states if you operate there |
| **Limited VC ecosystem** | Estonian companies are less familiar to US VCs than Delaware corporations; if raising US institutional capital, a Delaware C-Corp may be preferred |
| **Activity licences** | Regulated sectors require additional licences from Estonian authorities [12] |

## Source Reliability Notes

- **India fees:** The MCA "Enquire Fees" page states all figures are "indicative only" [9]. The binding fee schedule is the Table of Fees in the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014 as amended [40], and the live SPICe+ computation. MCA processing times are from a secondary source reporting MCA-published SLAs [36]; no primary MCA SLA page was accessible in the evidence set — treat these as reported, not verified from a live official page.
- **Estonia:** Key facts (€265 fee, 1-working-day processing, annual report deadline) are confirmed across multiple primary official sources [11][12][13][14][20].
- **Delaware:** Incorporation fees post-August 2026 are confirmed by the official Division of Corporations fee schedule PDF dated August 1, 2026 [27] and the official LLC Formation PDF [34]. Annual tax of $400 for LLCs is confirmed by multiple official Delaware sources [3][5][34] and corroborated by multiple secondary sources [15][17][23]. One low-quality source dated July 2026 still cited $300 [44], which appears to reflect the pre-2026-tax-year rate.
- **Standard processing time for Delaware:** The Division of Corporations does not publish an official standard (non-expedited) SLA for Certificate of Formation/Incorporation on the pages reviewed. Only expedited service times are officially stated [6]. This is **UNCLEAR** for standard filing.

claims.claim: Delaware charges LLCs a flat annual LLC tax of $300 per entity, not a percentage of income or assets, owed whether or not the LLC had activity that year.
claims.snippet: Delaware does not require LLCs to file an annual report the way corporations do. Instead, every domestic and foreign LLC registered in the state owes what Delaware calls the annual LLC tax. This is a flat fee, not a percentage of income or assets

claims.claim: Delaware's annual LLC tax due date is June 1 for LLCs, while Delaware corporations' franchise tax and annual report are due March 1.
claims.snippet: Delaware sets a single due date for every LLC, June 1. This differs from Delaware corporations, whose franchise tax and annual report are due March 1.

claims.claim: Missing the June 1 deadline triggers a $200 penalty on top of the $300 tax, with monthly interest of 1.5 percent on the unpaid balance.
claims.snippet: Total owed after a missed deadline = $300 tax + $200 penalty = $500, before monthly interest of 1.5 percent accrues on the unpaid balance.

claims.claim: As of July 2026 the Delaware LLC annual tax remains a flat $300 per entity, unchanged from prior years.
claims.snippet: As of July 2026, the Delaware LLC annual tax remains a flat $300 per entity, unchanged from prior years.

claims.claim: Delaware's statute reserves the term franchise tax for corporations under Title 8, while LLCs fall under a separate section calling their fee the annual tax.
claims.snippet: Franchise tax is technically the term reserved for corporations under Title 8 of the Delaware Code... LLCs and limited partnerships fall under a separate section of the code that simply calls their fee the annual tax.

claims.claim: Foreign LLCs registered to transact business in Delaware also owe the flat $300 annual tax, separate from home-state fees.
claims.snippet: If your LLC was formed in another state but you registered it as a foreign entity in Delaware... you still owe the flat $300 annual tax.

claims.claim: Delaware's registered agent fee is paid separately to a third party each year and is not part of the state annual tax.
claims.snippet: This is separate from federal income tax, separate from any state where your LLC actually operates and pays its own franchise or entity level fees, and separate from Delaware's registered agent fee that most owners pay to a third party service each year.
